transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (CloudBridge PM), Ethan Zhou (CloudBridge Marketplace Eng), Marta Lopez (CloudBridge Security)

[00:00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Samir and Lena from Redwood, and Priya, Ethan, Marta from CloudBridge, is that right?
[00:00:08] Priya Nair: Yep, that's right, thanks Alex.
[00:00:10] Samir Patel: Morning all, Samir here.
[00:00:12] Ethan Zhou: Ethan, hi.
[00:00:14] Marta Lopez: Marta on security.
[00:00:17] Alex Morgan: Great. Purpose today is to align on the marketplace listing requirements and the reference architecture for the joint integration — Redwood running as a managed offering on CloudBridge marketplace, plus optional private deployment for customers who buy through you. We'll walk through a proposed arch, security checklist, and the listing artifacts you need.

[00:00:35] Priya Nair: Sounds good. High level, our PM org wants to know what we need for the listing (images, docs, pricing), and our marketplace engineering team needs the deployment patterns — container image or SaaS link, VPC peering details, and the telemetry integration.

[00:00:50] Samir Patel: Quick context from Redwood side — we support three modes: hosted API (SaaS), Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For marketplace, most partners list our hosted offering first, but we can also provide a private deployment package that can be launched via an image or orchestrated via your marketplace provisioning.

[00:01:12] Ethan Zhou: Okay — for provisioning, CloudBridge supports both AMI/container images and a private marketplace flow where customers request a provisioning job and we spin up a tenant via CloudBridge managed infra. We'll need a deployable artifact and an automated playbook.

[00:01:28] Samir Patel: For the private option we usually provide a Helm chart + operator instructions, an infra playbook (VPC peering, subnets, security groups), and an optional bootstrap script to pull model weights from Redwood custody or a customer S3. Important: some customers require that model weights never leave their VPC — in those cases we recommend on-prem package or bring-your-own-weights workflow.

[00:01:52] Marta Lopez: On security, we need to confirm encryption and KMS flow. Customers will ask: do we support customer-managed keys, HSM, and SSE-KMS? Also audit logging and SOC 2 evidence.

[00:02:04] Alex Morgan: Yes, we support KMS integrations — Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for at-rest encryption and key wrapping. For hosted, we provide SOC 2 reports and an attestation; for Private we'll provide the deployment checklist and expected audit logs. We'll attach our security pack.

[00:02:22] Marta Lopez: Great, can you clarify network topology? For POC customers we need to validate VPC peering vs transit gateway patterns. Latency is a concern for synchronous inference.

[00:02:34] Samir Patel: For low latency we recommend VPC peering or colocated instances. If the marketplace provisioning uses private endpoints, we can do interface endpoints and private DNS. The reference arch I'll send will show 1) peering with private subnets hosting the inference cluster, 2) optional NAT for outbound model pulls, and 3) a bastion for ops.

[00:02:58] Priya Nair: On the listing side, we need marketing assets: short description, screenshots, a quickstart video, and the technical README. We support a 500 word overview and a separate integration guide link.

[00:03:12] Alex Morgan: We'll prepare a listing kit — short description, 3 screenshots (console, latency dashboard, endpoint config), a 2 minute quickstart, and a public integration guide. We'll also include a private deployment README for marketplace engineers.

[00:03:26] Ethan Zhou: For billing — do you want CloudBridge to handle charging for both hosted consumption and a reserved capacity SKU, or will Redwood bill directly?

[00:03:35] Lena Ruiz: We typically support both models. For marketplace convenience, we can do a bill-through option where you resell our hosted credits, or the partner can co-bill for the reserved capacity. We'll need to share pricing tiers and pricing variables (per-token, per-embedding).

[00:03:50] Alex Morgan: We'll send a pricing/practice sheet — sample SKUs, per-token estimates, and a recommended reserved-capacity bundle. Action: I'll share that by Tuesday.

[00:03:58] Priya Nair: Good. On certifications, CloudBridge requires SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 as marketplace minimums for managed listings. You mentioned SOC 2 is available. Do you have the other certs?

[00:04:08] Alex Morgan: We have SOC 2 Type II, and we're in progress on ISO 27001 — ETA Q3. For Private deployments customers get the control and we provide the compliance artifacts relevant to deployment. We'll attach the SOC 2 report in the package.

[00:04:20] Marta Lopez: We'll need the security questionnaire answered — I can send a standard CSV. Do you have a single point of contact for that?

[00:04:26] Alex Morgan: Marta, Samir will take point on the detailed security Q. I'll coordinate the non-technical attachments.

[00:04:32] Samir Patel: Yep, I'll handle the questionnaire. Quick note: some of the questions about KV cache and runtime exploitation sounded odd in prior templates — we'll answer with how our runtime manages KV caches and our network isolation model.

[00:04:44] Ethan Zhou: On telemetry, we need logs for provisioning status and health endpoints to surface in our marketplace console. Can Redwood expose a monitoring endpoint or push metrics to CloudBridge telemetry?

[00:04:55] Samir Patel: We can push metrics to Prometheus endpoints or expose OpenTelemetry metrics. For marketplace-managed clusters, we can add a sidecar that forwards metrics to your ingestion endpoint. We'll include sample Grafana dashboards too.

[00:05:10] Priya Nair: Nice. For the reference architecture doc, could you include a decision table for customers choosing hosted vs dedicated vs private? We want a simple guidance line for product pages.

[00:05:20] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We'll include a matrix: sensitivity of data, throughput needs, latency SLO, and cost tradeoffs. That will map to recommended deployment mode.

[00:05:30] Alex Morgan: Let's quick-run the proposed milestones so we're aligned: 1) Redwood sends listing kit and pricing/practice sheet by 2026-03-23, 2) CloudBridge sends marketplace template and security questionnaire by 2026-03-26, 3) Redwood returns security questionnaire answers and reference architecture by 2026-03-24, 4) POC kickoff week of 2026-04-06. Does that timeline work?

[00:05:50] Priya Nair: Yes that works assuming we get the template quickly.

[00:05:55] Marta Lopez: For the KMS requirement, do you support Bring-Your-Own-Key where the key never leaves the customer cloud? Some of our regulated customers mandate that.

[00:06:03] Samir Patel: For private deployments, yes. For hosted we have envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for enterprise tenants where possible — key material still managed by Redwood but wrapped with customer CMK. We'll document exact flow and limitations.

[00:06:18] Ethan Zhou: A couple of implementation questions from engineering: 1) what base OS and container runtime do you support, 2) what GPU drivers and CUDA versions are required for Dedicated/private?

[00:06:28] Samir Patel: We support Ubuntu 22.04 base, containerd / Docker, and require CUDA 12.x and NVIDIA driver 535+ for the latest optimized kernels. We'll include exact driver matrix. For quantized fallback we can run on CPU with degraded throughput.

[00:06:45] Priya Nair: About model licensing — if a customer uses Redwood to serve open models via the marketplace, are there any distribution limitations we should highlight?

[00:06:53] Alex Morgan: We'll add a short note: customers are responsible for model licensing if they bring their own weights. For our curated models offered by Redwood, licensing is cleared and documented. We'll include a section in the listing about model responsibilities.

[00:07:06] Ethan Zhou: For the marketplace UI, we display estimated latency and cost per 1k calls — can you provide sample benchmarks for a 512-token request on your hosted tier and a dedicated small/medium tier?

[00:07:18] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll include benchmark rows: hosted p50 p99 latency, and throughput for dedicated small (2x A10Gs), medium (8x A100s), plus cost per 1k tokens at typical batch sizes. Note caveat: numbers vary by prompt distribution.

[00:07:31] Priya Nair: Good. For joint solutions, we're thinking of a reference architecture that bundles CloudBridge provisioning + Redwood Private for enterprise customers. What marketing support do you need from us?

[00:07:42] Alex Morgan: Co-branded diagram, a joint solution brief, and a reference case study after the first POC. We'll share a template for the brief.

[00:07:50] Lena Ruiz: Another operational question — who handles support escalations for customers who buy through CloudBridge? Do we want to tie support channels?

[00:07:58] Alex Morgan: For hosted we handle L1/L2 and CloudBridge can escalate to us. For private deployments, we recommend a joint-support model where CloudBridge handles initial provisioning queries and Redwood handles runtime/performance bugs. We'll draft an escalation matrix.

[00:08:12] Marta Lopez: For logging and audit trails, we need to confirm retention windows. Some customers demand 12+ months. What's Redwood's default?

[00:08:20] Samir Patel: Default hosted retention is 90 days for operational logs, but enterprise tiers can request extended retention and archive to customer S3. We'll document retention options and costs.

[00:08:33] Priya Nair: Perfect. Anything else on the tech side?

[00:08:36] Ethan Zhou: One ask — can you provide a small demo script we can run in our CI to validate a marketplace-provisioned cluster? Something like health-check endpoints and a sample generation request.

[00:08:46] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll provide a small smoke-test script with curl commands against the health endpoint, a token refresh example, and a sample inference payload.

[00:08:56] Alex Morgan: Ok to recap and close: action items — Samir to draft reference architecture, runbook, driver matrix and security answers by 2026-03-24; Alex to send pricing and listing kit by 2026-03-23; Priya to send marketplace template and questionnaire by 2026-03-26; Marta to confirm KMS constraints and any additional compliance asks; schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-04-06.

[00:09:20] Priya Nair: Thanks all, that recap works. We'll want a follow-up invite once we have the docs.

[00:09:27] Alex Morgan: Great, we'll circulate notes and attach the files. Meeting's recorded. Thanks everyone.

[00:09:34] (end)

Notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts; speaker labels may be approximate. References to product names: Redwood Private/Dedicated/Hosted, KV cache, KMS, VPC peering, Helm chart, Prometheus/OpenTelemetry.
